Matt C: quick question — when an upstream produces a partial streaming payload and then errors mid-stream, what's our preferred gateway behavior? forward partial and close, attempt a hedged retry, or return a soft-failure + retry hint?
Sasha P: my vote: if the request is idempotent (no side-effects) we should try a short hedged retry to another healthy upstream variant. Otherwise return the partial and attach a retry hint. avoids duplicating side-effects. :thinking_face:
Jordan L: +1 but we need rules around cache/kv state. if completion depends on ephemeral KV we can't replay safely. also latency budget matters — hedged retry only if remaining deadline > N ms.
Linh T: agreed. propose a small surface: X-RW-Retry: soft|hard|no-retry and Retry-After when helpful. gateway sets it based on idempotency + side-effect metadata from the route. sample: 
```
X-RW-Retry: soft
Retry-After: 1
X-RW-Reason: upstream-partial-err
```
Matt C: good. also involvement for streaming: if we forward partial tokens then client has seen them — hedged retry might cause duplicated tokens if upstream sends overlapping content. how do apps dedupe?
Sasha P: we can emit an event header at the start of a stream: X-Stream-Seed: <id> and then hedged upstreams should attempt to continue from last emitted checkpoint if available. if not, they must produce a dedupe span. but that's complex.
Jordan L: that's why I prefer avoid automatic hedging for long streams. instead: if partial length < threshold (e.g., <1k tokens) we can attempt quick hedge; otherwise surface to client and mark retriable.
Linh T: add cost/billing note — if we hedge we should checkpoint billing to the first successful commit point. need clear semantics: payer shouldn't double-billed for duplicate in-flight attempts.
Matt C: good call. For observability and downward signals, can we include a short blob in traces that indicates why we returned partial? e.g., trace tag: proxy.abort_reason=upstream_stream_error and retry_hint=soft
ops-bot: canary deploy: proxy/edge v2.14.0 rolling to 10% — feature flag `stream-retry-hints` enabled in canary clusters.
Sasha P: another implementation detail: gateways must not swallow downstream trailers. if upstream sends a trailer error, we should map it to a structured reason and include both trailer and X-RW-Reason to client.
Matt C: agreed. final proposal summary: 
1) Determine idempotency & side-effect safety from route metadata.
2) If safe and remaining deadline > hedge_threshold -> attempt hedged retry (short, single extra try).
3) If not safe or stream > token_threshold -> return partial + set X-RW-Retry: soft or no-retry.
4) Always attach X-Stream-Seed and X-RW-Reason for observability; include Retry-After when appropriate.
5) Billing: checkpoint at commit points; ensure metrics mark hedged attempts separately to avoid double-charging clients.
Can we get +1s on this and a small follow-up PR to add header docs and the canary flag? :+1:
Jordan L: +1
Sasha P: +1, will draft the PR with header examples and a short test plan.
Linh T: +1, I'll add billing checkpoint notes to the billing runbook.
Matt C: thanks — I'll open the RFC follow-up and link to the canary.
ops-bot: noted. rolling canary progress: 6/10 clusters healthy.
